evidence: src/common/guard/jwt-auth.guard.ts: class JwtAuthGuard extends AuthGuard('jwt-strategy'), a framework request guard, which is a presentation responsibility

handleRequest maps TokenExpiredError to ForbiddenException('tokenExpired', StatusCodesList.TokenExpired) and a missing user to UnauthorizedException, which is error mapping at the transport boundary
No database access, domain rules or token-verification logic appear in the file
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file matches the presentation layer through its *.guard.ts file pattern. JwtAuthGuard is a NestJS request guard. It hands authentication off to the Passport 'jwt-strategy' and turns the result into HTTP-facing exceptions: Forbidden when the token has expired, Unauthorized when there is no user. Gating requests and mapping auth failures to transport errors is normal work for a presentation guard. The file has no business rules, no persistence and no token-verification logic. Verification itself is left to the strategy, which belongs to infrastructure.
